7734a0b850210db30aa0.title: Training Unit Director
7734a0b850210db30aa0.description:
*Training Unit Director*

National Child Trauma Programs

Organization: NC Youth Violence Prevention Center

Location: In Person, Hybrid or Remote/virtual within the United States; preference may be given to candidates based in North Carolina

Portfolio: Two SAMHSA National Child Traumatic Stress Initiative Category II projects

**Lead National Child Trauma Training and Innovation**

The NC Youth Violence Prevention Center is conducting a national search for an exceptional leader to serve as Training Unit Director and coordinate two five-year SAMHSA National Child Traumatic Stress Initiative Category II initiatives.

This is not a conventional training coordinator role. The Training Unit Director will help build, organize, and disseminate national resources designed to improve how evidence-based childhood trauma treatment is implemented in real-world settings. The successful candidate will manage multiple complex products and workstreams at the same time, coordinate nationally distributed partners and implementation sites, support virtual training and consultation, and work closely with the National Child Traumatic Stress Network and other leaders in childhood trauma treatment.

The Rural Trauma Treatment Implementation and Adaptation Center will strengthen the ability of rural clinicians and child-serving systems to implement and sustain TF-CBT, Bounce Back, trauma narrative work, caregiver engagement, and other evidence-based trauma practices. The project is designed to train at least 1,500 professionals, consult with 40 rural teams, develop at least 12 major implementation products, and disseminate resources nationally.

For a talented program leader interested in child trauma, implementation science, workforce development, technology, training, and national impact, this is an unusual opportunity to help build something important from the ground up.

**About NC YVPC**

NC-YVPC is a nationally recognized nonprofit dedicated to helping children, adolescents, families, and communities address trauma, violence, abuse, adversity, and other behavioral health challenges. Our work combines evidence-based clinical practice, community engagement, training, federal grant implementation, evaluation, technology, and creative approaches to reaching children and families.

We value professionals who can move comfortably between big-picture strategy and disciplined execution—people who can develop an exciting idea while also ensuring that the workplan, meeting schedule, participant roster, deliverable tracker, and follow-up assignments are accurate and current. The Training Unit Director will join a multidisciplinary team of clinical leaders, researchers, evaluators, technology specialists, trainers, implementation partners, and nationally recognized TF-CBT expertise.

**What You Will Lead**

The Training Unit Director will provide the operational and implementation leadership that connects both NCTSI Category II projects. The portfolio may simultaneously include:

* Virtual training academies, national webinars, learning collaboratives, office hours, and consultation cohorts
* Rural TF-CBT, Bounce Back, trauma narrative, caregiver engagement, and supervisor implementation resources
* Clinical decision aids, readiness checklists, fidelity tools, safety protocols, and implementation dashboards
* Expressive arts engagement materials, SEE-IT interactive training products, videos, and microlearning modules
* TF-CBT Workbook Coach implementation materials, responsible safeguards, privacy tools, and therapist-facing supports
* Toolkits, manuals, guides, implementation briefs, conference presentations, and national dissemination activities
* Field testing with clinicians, agencies, youth, and caregivers, followed by continuous quality improvement and product revision

Your job will be to move these ambitious initiatives from ideas to finished products—and from finished products into the hands of professionals who can use them.

**Primary Responsibilities**

Project and Portfolio Leadership

* Manage integrated workplans for both NCTSI Category II awards and maintain clear visibility across milestones, deadlines, dependencies, risks, staffing assignments, products, training events, implementation cohorts, and dissemination activities.
* Build and maintain project-management systems that show senior leadership what is on schedule, what needs attention, and what decisions are required.
* Coordinate concurrent product-development streams and keep clinical, technology, evaluation, communications, and implementation contributors aligned.
* Identify implementation barriers early and develop structured solutions before they threaten federal deliverables.

Training Unit Management

* Coordinate development and operation of NC-YVPC's national Virtual Training Academy, including asynchronous modules, webinars, learning collaboratives, office hours, consultation groups, supervisor training, and implementation coaching.
* Develop annual and quarterly training calendars and coordinate presenters, consultants, participants, learning cohorts, technical platforms, materials, evaluations, and follow-up.
* Help participants move beyond one-time training toward supported implementation, consultation, fidelity monitoring, and organizational sustainment.
* Support national recruitment of clinicians, supervisors, Child Advocacy Centers, schools, juvenile justice and child welfare partners, community behavioral health organizations, and other implementation sites.

Product Development

* Coordinate complex products from concept through drafting, clinical review, field testing, revision, approval, publication, and dissemination.
* Maintain product schedules and version-control systems across multiple simultaneous deliverables.
* Bring subject-matter experts, clinicians, evaluators, technology staff, designers, trainers, and implementation partners together around clear products and deadlines.
* Ensure products are practical, professionally presented, usable by frontline organizations, and delivered on schedule.

National Partner Engagement

* Serve as a key operational liaison with the National Child Traumatic Stress Network, participating NCTSI centers, national experts, professional organizations, and implementation sites.
* Coordinate advisory groups, expert meetings, implementation cohorts, product-review sessions, and partner communications.
* Build productive relationships with TF-CBT experts, rural providers, Child Advocacy Centers, schools, child welfare and juvenile justice partners, youth and caregivers, and other child-serving systems.

Implementation and Continuous Quality Improvement

* Coordinate pilot testing and structured feedback from clinicians, supervisors, implementation organizations, youth advisors, caregivers, and other stakeholders.
* Work with clinical and evaluation leadership to translate usability data, implementation outcomes, fidelity findings, and stakeholder feedback into product improvements.
* Support quarterly continuous quality improvement processes and ensure that decisions and corrective actions become changes in training, products, and implementation procedures.

Federal Award Coordination

* Maintain the operational documentation required for successful implementation of two major SAMHSA cooperative initiatives.
* Coordinate information for progress reports, performance measurement, evaluation, consultant documentation, training records, partner participation, and other federal deliverables.
* Work with the Project Director and administrative and fiscal staff to keep program activities aligned with approved workplans and federal expectations.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Two complex national initiatives operate as one coordinated portfolio rather than separate projects.
* Workplans, product trackers, calendars, documentation systems, and partner records remain current and useful.
* Major deliverables move through development, review, pilot testing, revision, and release without losing momentum.
* Training events and consultation cohorts are professionally organized and well attended.
* Partners receive timely communication and dependable follow-through.
* Clinical experts can focus on clinical content because the operational infrastructure around them works.
* Problems are surfaced early, and evaluation and continuous quality improvement findings lead to measurable improvements.
* NC-YVPC grows as a nationally visible source of high-quality child trauma training and implementation resources.

**The Candidate We Are Looking For**

We are looking for someone who is exceptionally organized without being bureaucratic, ambitious without losing attention to detail, and comfortable managing highly specialized contributors. The strongest candidates can coordinate a national webinar in the morning, facilitate a product-development meeting in the afternoon, identify a delay in an implementation workstream, communicate with a national partner, update a federal deliverable tracker, and still maintain a clear view of where two five-year initiatives are heading.

You should enjoy building systems, solving problems, bringing people together, and turning complicated projects into organized execution.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Master's degree in public administration, public health, social work, psychology, counseling, implementation science, or a closely related field preferred.
* Significant experience coordinating or managing complex programs, training initiatives, federally funded projects, behavioral health programs, nonprofit initiatives, research projects, or comparable multi-partner efforts.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent projects, products, deadlines, and contributors.
* Exceptional organizational, project-management, written communication, meeting facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Ability to develop and maintain sophisticated workplans, trackers, calendars, documentation systems, and follow-up processes.
* Ability to work effectively in a virtual environment with geographically dispersed staff and partners.
* Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and recognize when an issue requires escalation.

**Particularly Attractive Backgrounds**

We strongly encourage applications from candidates with experience in one or more of the following:

* SAMHSA, NCTSI, NCTSN, or other federal behavioral health initiatives
* Child trauma, children's behavioral health, TF-CBT, or other evidence-based interventions
* Training and technical assistance centers, continuing education, workforce development, or learning collaboratives
* Implementation science, Child Advocacy Centers, school mental health, rural behavioral health, child welfare, or juvenile justice
* Digital behavioral health, clinical technology, responsible AI implementation, or product development
* Project-management platforms, national nonprofits, or professional associations

Clinical licensure is not required. We are primarily seeking an outstanding program, implementation, training, and project-management leader who can work effectively alongside clinical experts.

**Why This Opportunity Is Different**

Few positions offer the chance to work simultaneously at the intersection of child trauma treatment, national training, implementation science, rural behavioral health, TF-CBT, technology, supervised AI, workforce development, and federal innovation.

The Rural Trauma Treatment Center is designed to convert field-tested rural trauma practice into reusable national infrastructure and tools that agencies can sustain after formal consultation ends. The Training Unit Director will have a meaningful role in shaping training initiatives.

**Work Location and Travel**

This position may be virtual or remote, allowing NC-YVPC to recruit nationally for the strongest candidate. Because NC-YVPC is headquartered in North Carolina and portions of product development, field testing, organizational collaboration, and implementation are anchored in the state, preference may be given to highly qualified candidates located in North Carolina or able to travel periodically to North Carolina.

Occasional national travel may be required for conferences, NCTSN and NCTSI activities, partner meetings, training events, or implementation work.

**What NC YVPC Offers**

* A significant leadership role in two national SAMHSA child trauma initiatives
* The opportunity to help build a growing NC-YVPC Training Unit
* Direct work with nationally recognized clinicians, researchers, evaluators, implementation specialists, and trauma-treatment experts
* Close collaboration with the National Child Traumatic Stress Network
* Leadership responsibility for innovative products with national dissemination potential
* A collaborative multidisciplinary environment with meaningful opportunities for professional growth, visibility, and leadership
* Remote-work flexibility and competitive compensation commensurate with qualifications and experience
* The opportunity to strengthen trauma-treatment capacity for children and families across the United States

**How to Apply**

Please submit a résumé and a cover letter describing your experience managing complex programs, training initiatives, or multiple concurrent projects. In your letter, tell us why this opportunity interests you and what experience you would bring to building and managing a nationally visible child trauma training portfolio.

Miranda Faircloth, Operations Director, NC Youth Violence Prevention Center, miranda.faircloth@ncyvpc.org

If you are a highly organized leader who enjoys turning ambitious ideas into well-executed programs—and you want your work to have national impact on the quality of trauma treatment available to children and families—we encourage you to apply.

Pay: $60,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance

Education:

* Master's (Required)

Work Location: Remote

7b83813dc124a23b62c3.description:
Stockton University is ranked among the top public universities in the Northeast with more than 160 undergraduate and graduate programs, as well as continuing education opportunities. Our University, one hour from Philadelphia and two hours from New York City, offers unique learning, living, and working environments throughout southern New Jersey, including the 1,600-acre Galloway campus in the Pinelands National Reserve and Atlantic City campus, located in the University District, just steps from the beach and iconic Atlantic City Boardwalk. Additional locations include Hammonton and Manahawkin.

As a public University, Stockton University provides an environment for excellence to our student body through an interdisciplinary approach to liberal arts, sciences, and professional education. Founded in 1969, our University held its first classes in 1971. Our University’s welcoming and vibrant community makes Stockton a great place to learn, live, and work! Learn more about the many reasons to choose Stockton at www.Stockton.edu. Our Faculty and Staff are committed to supporting Stockton University’s strong student-centered vision and mission.

### **Associate Dean, School of Education**

* Galloway, New Jersey

* School of Education

* Management

* Opening on: Oct 20 2026

**Campus Location:** Main Campus (Galloway)

**Department:** School of Education

**Salary Range:** $130,000 - $140,000

**Salary Information:** Salary commensurate with experience and is accompanied by an extremely competitive University benefits package

**University Pensions & Benefits Information Webpage**

**Work Hours:** Mon. - Fri. 9:00am - 5:00pm

**Brief Job Overview/Summary**

Reporting to the Dean of Education, the Associate Dean of Education serves as a key partner in advancing the School of Education’s academic, fiscal, and administrative priorities. The Associate Dean collaborates with the Dean to provide strategic leadership in curriculum and program development, accreditation and program review, assessment, faculty and staff recruitment and retention, and the advancement of research, scholarship, and grant activity. The Associate Dean also supports fundraising efforts and represents the School to senior administration, students, alumni, and internal and external constituents, alongside, and at the discretion of the Dean.

**Descriptions of Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Academic Leadership:**

* Collaborates with the Dean to provide innovative leadership and vision in the development, growth, and implementation of academic programs and policies within the School.
* Provides guidance on program planning, evaluation, curriculum development, and the assessment of student learning outcomes to promote continuous improvement.
* Working in collaboration with Chairs and the Office of Assessment, the Associate Dean collaborates to review programs, processes and recommends enhancements to academic offerings, including the integration of emerging technologies, in collaboration with the Dean.
* Ensures the achievement of strategic plan goals aligned with the School’s priorities as established by the Dean.
* Supports compliance with state and regional accreditation standards and specialized accreditation requirements for applicable programs.
* Promotes the expansion and quality of in-person, hybrid, and online programs, dual credit opportunities, and other innovative instructional initiatives.

**Faculty, Staff, and Student Success:**

* Supports the recruitment, development, and retention of excellent full-time faculty, adjunct faculty, and professional staff.
* Fosters an inclusive academic environment that emphasizes professionalism, excellence, integrity, and collaboration.
* Supports strategic enrollment initiatives, including student recruitment and retention, program marketing, and community engagement.
* Manages the resolution of student concerns related to instruction, grades, program requirements, and course scheduling.
* Assists in the training, mentoring, and professional development of School staff.
* Advances a scholarly environment aligned with the University's mission, values, and strategic priorities while enhancing the visibility and impact of the School’s educational, outreach, and research activities.

**Operations and Administration:**

* Assists the Dean and staff in developing and managing the School’s operating budget; supports resource planning, allocation, and expenditures.
* Maintains clear lines of communication among faculty, chairs, staff, students, and administrators to promote a collegial and supportive working and learning environment.
* In collaboration with the Dean, monitors School’s facilities to ensure offices, classrooms, and laboratories provide a safe, user-friendly environment for all occupants.
* Ensures compliance with state and federal regulations and University policies.

**External Relations and Institutional Engagement:**

* Serves as an active member of the Deans Council and represents the Dean in University-wide and School-wide meetings, committees, and leadership initiatives upon Dean’s request or absence.
* Partners with the Dean and Institutional Advancement to support fundraising initiatives that sustain programs and secure funding for scholarships, technology, and capital priorities, while encouraging public-private partnerships.
* Maintains productive relationships with alumni, donors, community leaders, and other stakeholders to support strategic improvement efforts.
* Represents the School of Education and the University at state and national meetings, conferences, and events.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

* Collaborative leadership skills with the ability to foster inclusive, high-performing teams and working relationships.
* Ability to communicate in an interpersonal, written, and oral manner across a complex academic community.
* Strategic thinking, analytical ability, and sound judgment in addressing complex organizational challenges.
* Ability to mentor, develop, and empower faculty and staff while promoting a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Experience in programmatic accreditation.
* Experience in fundraising and working with development and foundation teams.
* Experience securing and managing all components of grant funding, including proposal development, project development, team leadership, and grant administration.
* Ability to establish and sustain external partnerships with community stakeholders and organizations.
* Experience supporting student success.
* Ability to work in technology-rich environments, including support for online and hybrid education.
* Commitment to inclusive and academic excellence.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Earned doctorate from an accredited institution in a discipline aligned with the School’s academic programs.
* Five years of full-time teaching experience at a college or university, with a strong record of scholarship and service commensurate with the rank of Associate or Full Professor.
* Three years of progressively responsible administrative or faculty leadership experience, including engagement with strategic enrollment initiatives and student success efforts.
* Experience as a teacher and/or administrator in a P–12 setting, with demonstrated expertise in state licensure and regulatory requirements.
* Experience working in technology-rich environments, including support for online and hybrid education.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Demonstrated experience with recruitment and retention efforts.
* Engaged in and led significant work in programmatic accreditation.
* Experienced in fund raising and working with development and foundation teams.
* Experienced in all components of grant funding, from NGO, writing, project development, team building and leading, through directorship.
* Experienced identifying, building, and fostering external relations with community stakeholders and partners.

**Screening Information:**  
Screening of applications begins immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Applications received by (insert date below in Job Posting ) will receive full consideration.

**How to Apply:**
  
To apply please visit https://employment.stockton.edu

**Application Requirements:**  
Individuals who apply must complete the online application, provide names and contact information for three professional references, and submit the following required documents electronically in a Microsoft Word or PDF format:

* Letter of Interest/Cover Letter Describing Qualifications and Accomplishments
* Current Resume, Vita, or Curriculum Vitae
* Unofficial Graduate transcripts

**Important:**  
Individuals who apply must meet all Required Qualifications within the job advertisement to be considered for this position. Please note that any offer of employment is subject to, and contingent upon, completion of the University’s mandatory and favorable background check, which may include a consumer report, availability and receipt of appropriations from the State of New Jersey, and receipt of any required approvals by the University.

**SAME Program:**
  
In accordance with P.L. 2021, c. 465 and P.L. 2021, 466, the SAME Program permits eligible New Jersey State agencies and employers to consider qualified applicants for certain non-competitive and unclassified titles within the State workforce.

Applicants seeking consideration under the New Jersey SAME Program, must indicate that status when completing the online application. You must also submit the required SAME Program documentation for this specific position, as directed by the New Jersey Civil Service Commission, in addition to all required electronic documents for this position (e.g., cover letter, resume/vita/curriculum vitae, unofficial transcripts) on or before the closing date indicated above. Individuals who apply through the SAME Program must meet all Required Qualifications within the job advertisement to be considered for this position. For more information on the SAME Program, please contact the New Jersey Civil Service Commission by emailing SAME@csc.nj.gov.

a1d5e08d10a991ce69ac.description:
Job Description:

**Step into Your New Role**

Built on a foundation of excellence, Kleinfelder is committed to providing our clients with the best solutions with our best people within scope, schedule, and budget. We are engineers, scientists, and construction professionals servicing clients in several key markets, including transportation, energy, power, water, industrial, commercial, mining, and federal, state, and local government.

Through our depth of experience and thorough understanding of environmental, regulatory, economic, and civic conditions, we identify and address challenges with innovation and common sense. Kleinfelder’s integrated, award-winning experts collaborate with clients to meet their objectives, from project inception through design and execution. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose - together, we deliver.

**We are seeking a Division Director to lead our East Division, a dynamic business of more than 1000 professionals across thirty-six offices executing more than 5,300 projects annually for public and private sector clients. With annual revenues approaching $220 million, this role is responsible for driving profitable growth, strengthening client relationships, developing future leaders, and positioning the Division for long-term success. The successful candidate must bring prior, directly relevant experience leading a multi-office A/E/C business and be prepared to apply proven operating disciplines from day one. Candidates must reside in the East Division.**

The successful candidate will demonstrate a proven record of successful leadership developing, implementing, and successfully delivering a growth strategy through a deep understanding of our markets and services while achieving budgeted performance targets. He or she will be accountable for maximizing client satisfaction, managing risk, and meeting or exceeding budgeted targets for cash, sales, and profit in the Division. The successful candidate must be able to assess financial data quickly and make necessary changes to protect the interest of clients, employees, and shareholders.

**Division Leadership**

Demonstrate prior success owning and improving the full P&L of a geographically dispersed A/E/C operation.

* Meet or exceed Division budgeted targets for sales, revenue, cash and profit.
* Develop annual goals and budgets for the Division, related business units, and individuals.
* Lead the development of forecasting for sales, revenues, profitability, and resource requirements.
* Make a significant contribution to all Company-wide planning efforts, including periodic strategic planning, new business incubation gatekeeping, and development or revision of policies and procedures.
* Use exemplary interpersonal skills to develop people, build high-performing teams. and build client loyalty.
* Recruit the best technical expertise in our local markets to support the implementation of our strategy.

**Business Development**

* Establish and maintain executive-level relationships with key clients, strategic partners, and industry leaders.
* Identify emerging market opportunities and work to position Kleinfelder for success.
* Implement and reinforce efficient and effective programs to leverage client relationships, identify opportunities, develop plans for large-scale projects, and use client value propositions to win work.
* Create an annual Business Development Plan in alignment with the market strategy and plan.
* Engage with and participate in proposal teams, Red Team reviews and mock interviews for major pursuits to ensure the development of sound client value propositions.

**Operations**

* Develop and reinforce project management best practices and control to deliver client satisfaction and required profitability.
* Drive the quality of work product and technical excellence.
* Ensure the safety of employees through leadership and full execution of LPS.
* Coordinate with other Division Managers and Corporate personnel to ensure national and regional clients are serviced consistently and effectively.
* Serve as Principal-in-Charge for selecting key clients and large projects.

**Talent Management**

* Provide a challenging and rewarding environment for employees.
* Recruit, mentor, and coach senior team members and ensure this cascades down through the entire Division.
* Ensure the personnel in the Division comply with current policies and procedures.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering or science (environmental, geology, biology, chemistry, etc.) from an accredited college or university required. MBA preferred.

**Experience:** A minimum of twenty years of progressively responsible leadership experience, with a minimum of fifteen in an environmental, engineering, or construction services firm. Candidates must have previously served in a senior operating role with full P&L accountability for a multi-office A/E/C business unit. The successful candidate must be able to point to measurable results in profitable growth, margin improvement, cash performance, project delivery, risk management, and leadership-team development.

**Certification/Registration:** Registered Professional Engineer or equivalent preferred.

**Other Knowledge and Skills:**

* Strong understanding of A/E/C industry business models and market direction.
* Superior communication skills and in-depth knowledge of company operations, services, and differentiators.
* Solid working knowledge of teaming partners, competitors, and clients.
* Ability to identify key expansion areas.
* Demonstrated strategic thinking and vision skills.
* Solid understanding of Company’s areas of expertise and demonstrated ability to pursue and execute on a wide variety of service types.
* Ability to develop creative approaches to create and growth teaming partners and strategic initiatives.

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

**Move Forward with Kleinfelder**

Kleinfelder has been connecting great people to the best work since 1961. We are engineers, scientists, and construction professionals providing solutions that improve our clients’ transportation, water, energy, and other private infrastructure. As a responsive, cross-disciplinary team of bright, curious, and innovative problem-solvers, we are dedicated to doing the right thing, every day, on every project from over 110 offices in the US, Canada, and Australia. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose – together, we deliver.

**Progress with an Employer that Values You**

Kleinfelder is an inclusive organization free from discrimination. We are a stronger organization when we are a diverse workforce and believe that through diversity, equity, and inclusion comes creativity, innovation, and unity. We are proud to offer the following:

***Benefits:*** Kleinfelder offers an excellent compensation and benefits package, including: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid holidays. The expected salary range for the position is displayed in accordance with the Maryland & Massachusetts Wage Transparency Laws. Final agreed upon compensation is based upon individual qualifications and experience. Salary range: $170,000-$315,000.

***Career Development:*** We are committed to investing in the professional development of our staff, offering each employee every opportunity to grow, develop, and take control of their career paths. We support these efforts through reimbursements for continuing education as well as many of the expenses associated with trainings and certifications, and opportunities for career development through our internal Mentoring Program.

***Equal Opportunity:*** Kleinfelder is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minorities/Women/Disabled/Veterans. (Compliant with the new VEVRAA and Section 503 rules)

**NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY AGENCIES**

Please note that Kleinfelder does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Recruitment Fee Agreement, Kleinfelder will not consider or agree to payment for any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without a previously signed agreement, Kleinfelder explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. Any unsolicited resume, including those submitted to hiring managers, are deemed to be the property of Kleinfelder.

0fafb6eaf37655b66a1f.description:
Our office, K&K Endodontics, is seeking a talented Dental Assistant to join our busy specialty practice.

We are looking for a talented and skilled Dental Assistant to help us accomplish our mission to improve the lives of our patients by providing a world-class specialty experience for every patient. Here is what you need to know about the role, our team and why we could be the right next step in your career.

  

**Your Responsibilities**

You will ensure excellent patient service and lift administrative and basic dental tasks off the Dentist's shoulders. You will be focused on ensuring that the patients' needs, concerns, and questions are answered. You will help keep the patient relaxed and comfortable during their visit, being the patients go to resource during their visit which includes the following:

* Welcoming patients to the dental office
* Preparing patients for treatment, ensuring their comfort
* Selecting and set up instruments, equipment, and supplies
* Sterilizing instruments according to regulations
* Assisting the dentist through 4-handed dentistry
* Providing oral hygiene and post-operative care instructions
* Keeping the dental room clean and well-stocked
* Scheduling appointments and post op visits
* Maintaining accurate patient records
* Assisting with payment procedures

As one of the essential members of our office, you will also help to facilitate/coordinate other office responsibilities as needed.

  

**Your Background**

You are a resourceful dental assistant who loves helping patients receive the experience they deserve and helping the Dentist to provide it. You're excited by the prospect of a patient leaving your office in a healthier, stronger, and more comfortable / happier being, each and every day. You're a kind, passionate and collaborative problem-solver who is able to proactively adjust to shifting priorities, and values the chance to make an important impact.

You also have the following:

* At least 1+ year(s) of proven experience as dental assistant, specialty is preferred
* Knowledge of dental instruments and sterilization methods
* Understanding of health & safety regulations
* Ability to perform regulated non-surgical tasks
* Good computer skills
* Excellent communication and people skills
* A strong attention to detail
* Well-organized and reliable
* A high school diploma
* A certificate from an accredited dental assistant program (if required by law)
* An active state radiology license (if required by law)
* Must be able to assist patients safely in and out of chairs or treatment areas
* Must be able to maintain clinical positioning for extended periods
* Must be able to work around medical equipment and instruments
* Must be able to adhere to OSHA and infection control standards
* Must be able to perform repetitive hand and wrist movements
* Must be able to respond quickly in emergency situations

If this sounds like you, you will fit right in with the team!

  

**Why You Should Join Our Team**

A career with us is a chance to work with everyone involved in the future of Specialty dental care. Dental Assistants, Sterilization Technicians, Specialists, Office Managers, Patient Care Coordinators and many more all work together to improve the patient care experience and great clinical results.

We strive to build and maintain an environment where employees from all backgrounds are valued, respected, and have the opportunity to succeed. You will also find a culture of continuous learning and a commitment to supporting our team members in all aspects of their lives—at home, at work and everywhere in between.

  

**Your Benefits & Perks**

* BCBS Medical & Dental insurance Options
* VSP Vision Coverage
* Complimentary Life Insurance Policy (employee only)
* Short-term & Long-Term Disability
* Pet Insurance Coverage
* 401(k) plan w/match options
* HSA / FSA Account Access
* Identity Theft Protection
* Legal Services Package
* Hospital/Accident/Critical Care Coverage
* Paid Time Off

  

*1815 W 13th Street, Ste 7, Wilmington, DE 19806*

3e5db9382f5dff1c32f1.description:
### **General Information**

Location:

US-AZ - Phoenix

Position Type:

Full Time

Virtual Eligible:

Yes

Ref #:

7624

  

### **Description and Requirements**

At the University of Phoenix, we are committed to the future of work by providing a fully remote, work-from-home environment. This strategy enables us to attract top talent nationwide. Are you looking for a rewarding and fulfilling position that offers challenging work and the opportunity to make a significant impact while collaborating with a team of fun, innovative individuals? Would you prefer to work with an organization that positively contributes to the world? If so, we would love to hear from you!

  

Are you searching for a rewarding, fulfilling position that offers challenging work and the ability to make a big impact while working side-by-side with a team of fun, innovative people? Ideally, would you like this position to be with an organization that makes a positive contribution to the world? If so…we would love to hear from you!

  
  

**About Us**

University of Phoenix is a leading higher education institution founded in 1976 by Dr. John Sperling. Our mission is to improve the lives of our students, their families and future generations through higher education. Our values (which hopefully you share) are: Brave. Honest. Focused.

  

Our University values and embraces all team members and their unique perspectives. We fundamentally believe in fostering an environment which deeply respects, celebrates, and actively encourages a diverse workforce. We are committed to hiring – and learning from – those who share our passion to help others achieve their educational aspirations.

  

We offer excellent benefits, an effective recognition program, and outstanding learning and development tools, including tuition vouchers for employees and their qualified family members.

**About the Position**

The Manager, Payroll provides operational leadership and day-to-day administration of the University’s payroll function, ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant payroll processing for employees and faculty, including regular, off-cycle, and executive payroll. The position directly supervises payroll team, serves as a hands-on Workday Payroll subject matter expert, and oversees payroll managed services providers (Payroll, Tax, and Garnishments). The role maintains effective payroll controls, resolves complex issues, partners with HR, Compensation, HRIS, Finance, and Benefits, and drives improvements in payroll accuracy, efficiency, and employee service.

**What You'll Do**

1. Lead end-to-end payroll production and processing, including collection, calculation, entry, validation, and updating of payroll data; ensure accurate and timely regular, off-cycle, employee, faculty, and executive payroll and resolution of payroll exceptions.

2. Direct the issuance of paychecks and electronic payments; oversee payroll reconciliations, payroll and tax accounting, and bank account funding in partnership with vendors and Finance; ensure timely review and resolution of discrepancies.

3. Serve as a Workday Payroll subject matter expert and maintain payroll system and data integrity. Support hands-on payroll processing, troubleshooting, testing, configuration changes, integrations, releases, enhancements, and issue resolution in collaboration with HRIS and technical resources.

4. Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local payroll and tax regulations, including multi-state payroll, wage and hour requirements, tax levies, garnishments, and other involuntary deductions; maintain appropriate documentation and controls.

5. Oversee payroll managed services vendors for payroll processing, payroll tax, and garnishments; monitor deliverables and service levels, manage escalations, and coordinate adjustments, amendments, refunds, notices, and service issues.

6. Audit and approve reconciliations of quarterly and annual payroll tax returns, W-2s, and third-party sick pay; oversee year-end activities and maintain effective approval processes, audit support, and payroll control procedures.

7. Select, mentor, coach and evaluate staff; establish and monitor appropriate employee performance objectives; prepare and present employee performance discussions, including one-on-one meetings and quarterly check-ins; implement mentoring and coaching plans, or correction action, where appropriate.

8. Perform other duties as required or apparent.

NOTE: The Primary Accountabilities above are intended to describe the general content and requirements of the position and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. Incumbents may perform all or most of the Primary Accountabilities listed above. Specific goals or responsibilities will be documented in incumbents’ performance objectives as outlined by the incumbents’ immediate manager.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Directly supervises the payroll team and provides day-to-day operational direction and oversight of payroll managed service providers.

**Minimum Education and Related Work Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Human Resources, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

* Five (5) years of progressively responsible payroll experience, including complex payroll operations and multi-state payroll.

**Additional Qualifications**

* Experience with Workday

* Seven (7) or more years of progressively responsible payroll experience and previous direct supervision and development of payroll employees.

* Demonstrated hands-on experience with Workday Payroll, including payroll processing, troubleshooting, testing, and supporting system changes.

* Experience leading payroll operations, projects, and/or employees.

* Strong knowledge of federal, state, and local payroll requirements, including payroll taxes, garnishments, and related compliance obligations.

* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills; ability to manage competing deadlines and resolve complex, sensitive payroll issues accurately.

* Effective written and verbal communication and collaboration skills across HR, Compensation, HRIS, Finance, Benefits, and external providers.

* Ability to maintain confidentiality of payroll and employee information and exercise sound judgment

* Experience with Workday Payroll reporting, calculated fields, business processes, configuration, integrations, releases, enhancements, and automation.

* Experience managing third-party payroll, payroll tax, and garnishment service providers and monitoring vendor service levels.

* Experience in a large, complex, multi-state organization, including executive payroll and complex compensation arrangements.

* Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) designation.

* Experience developing payroll reporting, metrics, reconciliations, internal controls, audit documentation, and process improvements.

*University of Phoenix is an equal opportunity employer.*

*If you are an active-duty military member seeking employment when off-duty, compliance with Department of Defense Joint Ethics Regulation, 5500-7-R, is required prior to starting employment with University of Phoenix. You are advised to contact your base Judge Advocate General to seek such approval and answer any questions.*

**Pay Range**

  

The annual pay range for this position is $87,600 (minimum), $132,300 (midpoint), and $177,000 (maximum).\*

\*Typical hiring range is between the minimum and midpoint of the above pay range. Actual starting base pay may vary based on factors such as education, experience, skills, location and budget. Compensation above the midpoint is generally associated with experienced, long-tenured employees who have demonstrated sustained performance and expertise in the role.

  

Individuals in this role are eligible for:

* Annual Bonus Award

Your work is critical to helping adult learners achieve their dreams, and we’re committed to rewarding you for your efforts. We offer a competitive, comprehensive total rewards package designed to help you achieve your health, financial, educational and work-life balance goals.

Full-time employees are eligible for:

* Medical, dental and vision plans; Flexible Spending Accounts; Health Savings Accounts; Life and Disability insurance; and our Wellness incentive program;
* Competitive 401(k) employer match;
* Substantial tuition discount for you and eligible dependents; and,
* A generous time off package, including paid vacation, sick time and company holidays.\*

  
  
  

Application Deadline is 10/28/2026.

*The University does not discriminate in its employment practices or in its educational programs or activities on the basis of sex/gender. Sexual harassment, sexual assault, dating and domestic violence, and stalking are forms of sex discrimination, which are prohibited under Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 and by University policy. Reports of misconduct, questions regarding Title IX, and concerns about noncompliance should be directed to the Title IX Coordinator:*

  
  

*Kelly Hermann, Vice President, Accessibility & Student Affairs*

*4035 S. Riverpoint Parkway*

*Phoenix, AZ 85040*

5c21a0946f922127e036.description:
Clearance Level

None

Category

Program Delivery and Execution

Location

Remote, Working from the USA

Key Skills For Success

Clinical Setting

Employee Management

Patient Care

Regulatory Compliance

##### **REQ#:****RQ230928**

##### **Public Trust:****None**

##### **Requisition Type:****Regular**

##### **Your Impact**

Own your opportunity to be on the frontlines of health innovation. Deliver for America’s health agency missions and enhance lives for hundreds of millions every day.

**Job Description**
-------------------

**GDIT is Your Place**

Make it your own by discovering new ways to apply the latest technology and processes. Own your opportunity at GDIT and be a meaningful part of improving how agencies operate. Our work depends on an experienced **OPTN Case Manager** joining our team to support the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA).

**Program Overview**

The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) aims to improve health outcomes by enhancing access to quality services, developing a skilled health workforce, and implementing innovative programs that benefit geographically isolated, economically or medically vulnerable populations. HRSA focuses on increasing health equity and strengthening local health systems through initiatives such as community health centers, the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN), the Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program, and support for maternal and child health.

**Position Summary**

At GDIT, we foster a people-centric environment. The **OPTN Case Manager** serves as the primary coordinator for monitoring, compliance, patient safety, and performance improvement activities involving OPTN member institutions, including transplant hospitals, Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs), and histocompatibility laboratories.

This role is responsible for managing the complete case management lifecycle, including intake, triage, investigation, tracking, analysis, review, resolution, and follow-up. The Case Manager collaborates with HRSA, OPTN committees, member organizations, and contractors to investigate potential policy violations, evaluate patient safety concerns, assess member compliance, and support corrective actions and process improvements.

The ideal candidate combines clinical expertise, case management experience, project coordination skills, strong analytical abilities, attention to detail, and the ability to effectively manage complex case reviews involving multiple stakeholders.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**Case Management & Clinical Review**

* Manage the secure intake and documentation of patient safety and compliance cases from all reporting sources.
* Assess newly submitted cases for severity, urgency, complexity, and potential patient impact.
* Develop case review plans, including timelines, data requirements, and stakeholder involvement.
* Conduct comprehensive and well-documented case reviews to ensure fair and consistent evaluation of compliance and patient safety concerns.
* Coordinate information gathering, documentation reviews, interviews, and other activities required to evaluate assigned cases.
* Escalate cases as appropriate and coordinate external reviews with organizations such as the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).
* Monitor and track implementation of corrective actions, including Corrective Action Plans (CAPs).

**Case Coordination & Stakeholder Management**

* Coordinate case-related activities among HRSA, OPTN committees, member organizations, contractors, and other stakeholders.
* Facilitate communication among stakeholders throughout the case lifecycle.
* Ensure stakeholders receive timely updates regarding case status, documentation requirements, and follow-up activities.
* Document stakeholder roles, responsibilities, and coordination requirements associated with assigned cases.
* Support implementation of case review plans and resolution activities.
* Participate in cross-functional meetings and stakeholder engagements related to case review and compliance activities.

**Compliance, Quality, and Process Improvement**

* Analyze case information to identify trends, patterns of non-compliance, operational risks, and patient safety concerns.
* Develop recommendations for process improvements, policy enhancements, educational initiatives, and corrective actions.
* Provide insights and recommendations to HRSA and other stakeholders regarding compliance risks and mitigation strategies.
* Support continuous quality improvement initiatives related to case management workflows and oversight processes.
* Review historical case data and operational findings to identify opportunities for process improvement.
* Recommend strategies to strengthen oversight, accountability, and compliance among OPTN member organizations.

**Project Coordination & Administration**

* Manage multiple concurrent cases and priorities while ensuring timely progression and resolution.
* Track case milestones, deliverables, deadlines, and follow-up activities.
* Coordinate activities with internal teams, contractors, and external stakeholders as necessary to support case review and resolution.
* Maintain accurate documentation of case activities, findings, and outcomes.

**Documentation, Reporting & Record Management**

* Ensure appropriate handling, redaction, storage, and transfer of sensitive information and records.
* Maintain accurate and complete case documentation in accordance with established procedures.
* Develop and maintain case tracking tools and systems to monitor case status, metrics, milestones, and outcomes.
* Prepare recurring and ad hoc reports for HRSA, OPTN committees, and other stakeholders.
* Draft comprehensive case reports summarizing findings, decisions, recommendations, and follow-up actions.

**Technical & Data Management**

* Utilize case management and tracking systems to maintain accurate records and reporting.
* Analyze case and operational data to support decision-making and trend identification.
* Ensure stakeholders have timely access to information needed to support case review and resolution activities.
* Support enhancements to case tracking, reporting, and workflow management tools.
  

**Required Qualifications**

**Clinical & Case Management Experience**

* Clinical degree required, such as:
  + Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
  + Registered Nurse (RN)
  + Medical Doctor (MD)
  + Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO)
  + Physician Assistant (PA)
  + Other relevant clinical degree and licensure
* Minimum of six (6) years of experience in case management, clinical review, quality improvement, auditing, investigations, compliance, transplantation, or related healthcare operations.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex healthcare cases involving multiple stakeholders.
* Experience reviewing and interpreting clinical information and assessing potential patient safety concerns.

**Project Coordination & Organizational Skills**

* Strong project coordination and organizational skills.
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to documentation accuracy.
* Ability to independently organize, prioritize, and manage assigned work.

**Communication & Interpersonal Skills**

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to communicate effectively with clinicians, healthcare administrators, federal staff, contractors, and other stakeholders.
* Strong collaboration, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to present findings, recommendations, and case outcomes in a clear and professional manner.

**Technical Skills**

* Strong computer skills and demonstrated proficiency with:
  + Microsoft Word
  + Microsoft Excel
  + Microsoft PowerPoint
  + Microsoft Outlook
  + Microsoft Teams
* Experience using case management, compliance tracking, reporting, or workflow management systems.
* Ability to analyze and interpret data to support operational and compliance activities.

**Professional Requirements**

* Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism.
* Ability to travel throughout the United States up to 15% of the time.
* Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in transplantation, organ donation, organ procurement, or related healthcare fields.
* Experience working with transplant centers, Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs), histocompatibility laboratories, or similar organizations.
* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or other project management certification.
* Experience supporting federal healthcare programs, quality oversight programs, accreditation activities, or regulatory review processes.
* Familiarity with OPTN operations, member compliance activities, patient safety reviews, or performance monitoring processes.

**Description**
---------------

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and secure technological solutions to enable strategic objectives. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we will support yours by expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you will have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career.

Northrop Grumman’s Corporate Sector's Chief Information & Digital Office (CIDO) is seeking a **Senior Principal Technical Services Project Management**

to support IT Infrastructure and Operations (ITIO) organization. The selected candidate will act as a Special Projects Execution Lead to drive coordination, governance, and disciplined delivery across a portfolio of complex, cross‑functional initiatives. In this highly visible role, you will own portfolio cadence, reporting, and communications, while coaching ITIO teams and vendors to strengthen delivery rigor, risk management, and operational readiness.

  

This position directly supports CIDO and ITIO leadership in achieving critical cost, schedule, and performance objectives. The ITIO organization is managing a rapidly expanding portfolio of complex, cross‑functional initiatives that demand consistent coordination, strong governance, and disciplined execution. To meet this need, we are establishing a dedicated Execution & Coordination Lead to provide structured oversight for high‑priority efforts, including Dell Transformational License Agreement (TLA) utilization, Broadcom Enterprise Agreement (EA) utilization, client/server patching improvements, and critical operational initiatives. The initial focus of this role will be driving utilization, communication, coordination, reporting, and planning related to the Dell TLA and Broadcom EAs.

This role will own cadence, reporting, and communications across ITIO, vendors, and stakeholders, ensuring that resources are allocated to the highest‑value work, risks and issues are actively managed, and changes are implemented predictably and transparently.

In addition, this role will accelerate delivery and strengthen rigor across all ITIO efforts, serving as the central coordinator for ITIO strategic initiatives as they arise. The Senior Principal Technical Services Project Management role will partner with our Governance and Strategy organization to standardize lightweight project approaches and agile practices, and will provide leadership in status reporting, risk management, and dependency visibility. Through these responsibilities, the role will reduce operational risk, improve cost efficiency, and increase overall delivery reliability. Rather than duplicating the work of the Project Management organization, this position will complement it by applying execution discipline within ITIO’s operational context and ensuring that ITIO’s strategic and operational initiatives are delivered consistently and with measurable business value

*This is a virtual/remote role, however the preferred candidate will work eastern standard hours and preferably live on the east coast.*

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Portfolio Governance & Reporting**

* Serve as the central point for project, program, and operational initiative tracking and reporting within IT Infrastructure and Operations (ITIO), bringing consistent rigor to the management and oversight of initiatives.
* Establish and maintain portfolio‑level dashboards and status reporting to provide leadership with clear visibility into progress, risks, issues, and dependencies across ITIO initiatives.
* Lead and coordinate Project Management Reviews (PMRs) and other recurring governance forums, ensuring status, issues, and decision needs are communicated to stakeholders in a timely and concise manner.

**Risk, Issue, and Dependency Management**

* Identify, track, and drive resolution of risks, issues, and opportunities across the ITIO portfolio, including escalation and coordination with CIDO and Global Operations as appropriate.
* Ensure clear ownership, due dates, and follow‑through on risk and issue mitigations, including cross‑functional dependencies and vendor-delivered work.

**Operational Readiness & Change Management**

* Engage with other CIDO service line teams to plan, deploy, and integrate new capabilities and initiatives that impact ITIO, with a focus on operational readiness, supportability, and change management.
* Partner with HR and Communications to plan and execute communication and change‑management activities for major ITIO initiatives.

**Technical / Tooling Skills**

* Experience with enterprise PM/Agile tooling (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps, Rally, Clarity, ServiceNow, or equivalent) for portfolio tracking, backlog management, and reporting.
* Familiarity with IT infrastructure and operations domains (e.g., endpoint management, networking, cloud platforms, identity & access management, observability/monitoring).
* Experience with ITIL/ITSM practices (incident, problem, change, and configuration management) and how they intersect with project and program delivery.

**Governance, Risk & Compliance**

* Experience designing and operating governance cadences across multiple initiatives (steering committees, PMRs, risk reviews).
* Strong risk management discipline, including IF/DUE TO/BY/THEN risk articulation, contingency planning, and mitigation tracking.
* Familiarity with regulatory, security, or audit requirements that impact IT infrastructure and operations.

**Leadership & Stakeholder Management**

* Proven ability to influence without direct authority and drive alignment across diverse stakeholders (IT, HR, Communications, vendors, business partners).
* Demonstrated experience leading cross‑functional teams through change, including adoption of new processes, tools, or operating models.
* Strong relationship‑building skills with internal partners (e.g., HR, Communications, Finance, Global Operations) and external vendors.

**Communication & Change Management**

* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to distill complex technical and operational issues into executive‑ready messaging.
* Experience planning and executing change‑management and communications activities in partnership with HR and Communications (e.g., stakeholder analyses, communication plans, training materials).
* Ability to create and maintain clear, concise artifacts (roadmaps, one‑page summaries, FAQs, decision logs) that support executive visibility and workforce adoption.

**Operational Excellence & Analytics**

* Experience defining and tracking KPIs for IT operations and project execution (e.g., cycle time, SLA adherence, change success rates, backlog health).
* Ability to analyze data and trends to identify opportunities for process optimization and cost/schedule/performance improvements.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* 8 Years of relevant experience with Bachelors; 6 Years with Masters; 4 Years with PhD.
* Experience working with Global Supply Chain and Business Management.
* Demonstrated program/project management experience using Traditional Waterfall, Agile, and/or Hybrid methodologies on complex, cross-functional IT initiatives.
* Prior experience managing a portfolio of diverse and complex IT projects/initiatives, including cross‑functional dependencies and vendor‑delivered work.
* Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior leadership and cross‑functional teams in a matrixed environment.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with IT Disaster Recovery (ITDR) and information security governance, including coordination with security, compliance, or audit stakeholders.
* Scrum Master certification (e.g., Scrum Inc, Scrum Alliance, SAFe, Scrum@Scale, etc.) and/or PMP certification.

* Experience working with Sector-CIDO and/or Sector Program Teams.
* Demonstrated ability to proactively identify issues, propose actionable solutions, and drive issues rapidly to closure, including risk and dependency management.
* Demonstrated ability to communicate, present, and collaborate with executive leadership, including preparation of clear, concise status reports and briefings.
* Previous experience managing budgets or financials and partnering with business stakeholders to prioritize support aligned to business priorities and objectives.
* Experience establishing and operating portfolio‑level governance, including cadence definition, dashboards, and standardized reporting.
* Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with the ability to synthesize complex information and translate it into clear recommendations.
* Experience managing projects using ServiceNow.

We offer flexible work arrangements, phenomenal learning opportunities, exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly team environment. At Northrop Grumman, we are on the cutting edge of innovation. Our diverse portfolio of programs means there are endless paths to cultivate your career. We also offer exceptional benefits/healthcare, a 9/80 work schedule, and a great 401k matching program. Come join us!

Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results.
